exercise.name: Hanging Knees to Elbows

reference.title: Hanging Knees to Elbows
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; page could not be read at authoring time, movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip and knee flexion with a strong posterior pelvic tilt and spinal flexion; shoulder extension in a hang)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the knees drive up, inhale on the way down.
breathing.cadence: About 1.4 s up, 0.4 s hold, 2.2 s down

prescription.progression: Strict reps without swing, then a pause at the top, then toes to bar

cues.text: Hang from the bar with a wide overhand grip, arms straight.
Pull the shoulder blades down and press the bar toward the thighs (lats on).
Drive the knees up and curl the pelvis so the knees travel up to the elbows.
Touch knees to elbows (or as close as you can) and pause.
Lower slowly to the hang without swinging.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging to get the knees up
mistakes.fix: Pause in the hang and set the shoulders before each rep.

mistakes.mistake: Only lifting the knees to hip height
mistakes.fix: Curl the pelvis up; the knees go to the elbows.
Some elbow bend at the top is normal; drive the knees up with the abs and press the bar toward the hips rather than pulling the chin up.

kinematics.peak: ≈130° at the top (joint channel); thighs 25° above horizontal (hip to ankle line)
kinematics.norm: Deep flexion, thighs toward the chest (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Pelvis curls up: about 96° of spinal flexion (low back 44°); trunk -18° back from vertical, centre of mass within 10.3 cm of under the hands
kinematics.norm: Pelvis curls up into spinal flexion (clinical opinion; Escamilla 2006)

kinematics.setup: 115 cm (knee joint to elbow joint) in the hang
kinematics.peak: 17 cm joint to joint at the top: the knees arrive just below and inside the elbows (knee 8.1 cm lower), elbows bent about 42°
kinematics.norm: Knees reach the elbows (or as close as you can) at the top (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Hang 0.6 s, set the shoulders 0.3 s
kinematics.peak: About 1.4 s up, 0.4 s hold, 2.2 s down, 0.7 s hang
kinematics.norm: About 1.4 s up, 2.2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #13961, Hanging Knees to Elbows, video (movement reference)
Escamilla et al. 2006, electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training (Phys Ther 86(5):656-671; PubMed 16649890)
Andersson, Nilsson, Ma and Thorstensson 1997, abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises (Eur J Appl Physiol 75:115-123; PMID 9118976)
Axler and McGill 1997, low-back loads over a variety of abdominal exercises: searching for the safest abdominal challenge (Med Sci Sports Exerc 29(6):804-811)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Shoulder pain in the hang: build up with dead hangs and hanging knee raises.
Hanging leg and knee raises load the low back through the hip flexors (Axler 1997); avoid with acute back pain.
Use a bar you can reach without jumping, and step down rather than drop.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the pelvis up to bring the knees to the elbows; hanging knee and leg raises gave some of the highest rectus abdominis activity (Escamilla 2006).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Pull the thighs up to the chest (Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Assist the curl and stop the body twisting.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Press the straight arm toward the hips so the trunk tips back and the elbows meet the knees.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Control the shoulder blade under the hang.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Control the shoulder blade under the hang.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Long head helps extend the shoulder.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Long head helps extend the shoulder.

guides.label: Knees travel up to the elbows
